summary: The remaining gap asks whether the off-main-thread heartbeat write can produce a harmful outcome, and last turn I recorded that the candidate I care about most - the main loop's unguarded read-modify-write of the term being overwritten by a higher term written off-thread - had no deterministic witness because the window is only a couple of instructions. This turn removes that obstacle without touching production code: because the harness supplies the stable store, it can hold the store's write of the current term open at exactly the point that follows the main loop's read of the term and its computation of the next one, which is the real window widened rather than invented. The rest of the sequence is ordinary: the node is deposed by a real empty heartbeat with a higher term so its own election timer starts an election, the gate opens when that election reaches setCurrentTerm, one empty heartbeat with a term ten above the current one is delivered on the fast path while the write is held and is persisted and applied in memory, and then the held write is released so the election's lower term lands on top. The operands that decide the question are the in-memory and persisted terms immediately after the heartbeat and immediately after the release: if the term after release is lower than the one already adopted and persisted, the node has been returned to a term it had left, durably, which is the harmful outcome the gap asked about, while an unchanged term or a gate that never opens would defeat the suspicion or leave the run inconclusive, and I will say which once the receipt exists. I recorded the refined hypothesis and the discriminator on the same investigation rather than opening a new one, since this is the same handler and the same responsibility, and I assert nothing until the execution reports. The five witnessed findings from earlier turns remain recorded and unaffected, and both files validate.
